blocks.text: A secure image runs as non-root, contains no secrets, uses a pinned but continuously updated minimal base, and is scanned with sensible gates.

items: Non-root numeric USER, root-owned read-only code, writable dirs only where needed; at runtime `--read-only --tmpfs /tmp`.
No secrets in layers: strict .dockerignore, BuildKit secret mounts, runtime injection.
Pin base by digest and deps by hashed lockfile; Renovate/Dependabot move the pins.
Minimal runtime: no compilers, curl, package managers or shells if possible.

blocks.text:
$ trivy image --severity HIGH,CRITICAL --ignore-unfixed --exit-code 1 rag-api:1.4.2
$ docker scout cves rag-api:1.4.2

items: Gate on fixable HIGH/CRITICAL; track the rest.
Most findings come from base OS packages; slimmer bases remove whole classes.
Unreachable CVEs: document with VEX rather than muting the scanner.

blocks.text: Q: "How do you secure a container image?" A: "Non-root user and read-only rootfs; no secrets in layers via .dockerignore and secret mounts; a minimal base pinned by digest with automated updates; CI scanning that fails on fixable criticals; dropped capabilities at runtime."

items: Every layer is extractable: no secrets.
